newsitem.title: UK: London gold weakens to fresh low at fix.
newsitem.headline: London gold weakens to fresh low at fix.

text.p: The gold price sank to its lowest level since March 2, 1995 on Monday and market professionals are betting on it dipping further, dealers said.
Gold was fixed at $375.10 per ounce, down from $377.00 on Friday. It was the lowest fixing since $374.75 in March 1995.
"We are at new lows for the year and if it goes beyond $375, it could get very ugly," one dealer said.
He added that the professionals were largely sellers. "They are betting that $375 will not hold," the dealer said.
A break through $375 could take gold to around $372 quickly, below which support looked thin, a dealer said.
Adding significance to the $375 figure was a large volume of options at that strike due to expire at the over-the-counter options expiry this week, dealers said.
Gold has been under pressure from institutional and producer selling for several days and that pattern continued in the Far East ahead of the London opening, they said.
"The firmer dollar against the yen also brought out some long liquidation from Japan," a dealer said.
In Europe currencies were also shaky following Italy's return to the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), the dealer added.

A thinly traded market was forecast for this week given that New York's Nymex futures market would be closing early on Wednesday and would remain closed until the following Monday for the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday.
"So what happens during the rest of the week will really be decided on Wednesday afternoon," one dealer said.

Technical analysts said the medium-term prospect for gold was a decline to the critical $370 support level, which provided support going back to 1994, following the fall below the important $377 area last week.
Silver prices were also being treated warily although trade was thin and barely moved all morning from a $4.83/$4.85 opening, five cents below Friday's close.
Dealers said silver was vulnerable after heavy buying last week took the price to $4.98, at which point confidence ran out and the price went into retreat.
"There are a lot of disappointed longs in silver. The market is still broadly in a $4.75-$4.95 range," a dealer said.
Little interest was shown in platinum and palladium, which were steady at $381.75/$382.75, down $1.20, and $117.25/$118.25, up $0.65 respectively.
